mbp.overview: Maltose-binding protein captures sugars in the bacterial periplasm and delivers them to the MalFGK₂ importer. Its two domains surround a binding cleft whose accessibility changes as the domains move.

steps.title: Capture
steps.text: The interdomain cleft accommodates a sugar; domain closure can enclose the ligand.

steps.title: Deliver
steps.text: MBP engages MalFGK₂ and opens during transfer of the sugar to the membrane transporter.

steps.title: Transport
steps.text: ATP-driven changes in the transporter support uptake into the cytoplasm. MBP provides recognition and delivery; the transporter supplies the ATP-powered transport cycle.

reading.title: Scientific figure
reading.text: The primary reference pair is 3PUW and 1FQC. Blue and purple denote two conformational states, with experimental structures in gray. The RMSD plot measures similarity to each reference; the pocket surfaces and W62–W340 distance illustrate cleft opening.

reading.title: Animation
reading.text: The introductory cartoon explains sugar recognition and delivery to the transporter. The structural sequence uses 3PUW and 1FQC as the primary pair; 1FQB separately supplies the maltotriitol binding pose.

mbp.interpretation: The structural morph connects independently predicted conformations for viewing. Sugar approach is illustrative. Maltotriitol is a reduced sugar analogue used to show binding, not evidence that this analogue is transported.

bsppase.overview: Bacillus subtilis inorganic pyrophosphatase breaks down pyrophosphate (PPi), a product of many biosynthetic reactions, into two phosphate ions. Its catalytic cleft sits between two domains linked by a flexible hinge.

steps.title: Open the cleft
steps.text: Relative domain motion changes access to the active site, allowing substrate to enter.

steps.title: Organize the active site
steps.text: Substrate binding and metal coordination help position the phosphate groups and catalytic water.

steps.title: Hydrolyze PPi
steps.text: Metal-assisted hydrolysis converts pyrophosphate into two inorganic phosphate ions.

reading.title: Scientific figure
reading.text: The primary reference pair is 1K23 and 1WPM. Compare the blue and purple domain arrangements with their gray experimental references. The two-reference RMSD plot separates reference-like states, and the lower profile locates residues with different Cα displacements.

reading.title: Animation
reading.text: The opening cartoon explains PPi hydrolysis. Domain motion is illustrated using 1K23 and the metal-free 1WPM reference. The aligned PNP analogue and Mg²⁺ positions are supplied separately by 2HAW; 1K23 itself contains Mn²⁺ sites.

bsppase.interpretation: The video illustrates domain accessibility and catalytic geometry. The reaction cartoon is a schematic, and the aligned substrate analogue does not represent a simulated chemical reaction.

bbfpn.overview: BbFpn is a bacterial ferroportin homologue from Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus. It transports divalent transition-metal ions through a central cavity between two membrane-spanning lobes.

steps.title: Receive a metal ion
steps.text: An inward-facing cavity exposes the binding region to the intracellular side.

steps.title: Switch accessibility
steps.text: Rearrangement of the lobes and local helices changes which side of the membrane can reach the central cavity.

steps.title: Expose the outer route
steps.text: An outward-facing conformation provides access from the extracellular side, illustrating the alternating-access principle.

reading.title: Scientific figure
reading.text: The reference-state comparison uses 5AYM and 6BTX. The RMSD clusters distinguish alternative conformations; the local segment views and Cα profile show where the two states differ.

reading.title: Animation
reading.text: The outward-like comparison uses 5AYM; the retained inward-facing protein overlay uses 6BTX. The 6BTX entry also supplies Ca²⁺ and Ni–EDTA context, although the separate complex scene is omitted from the current video.

bbfpn.interpretation: The ion route is a geometric illustration through different access states. It does not measure ion flux or provide a timed transport trajectory.

pb2-4ncm.overview: The influenza A PB2 cap-binding domain recognizes capped RNA and is a target for small-molecule inhibitors. This case focuses on the inhibitor-bound domain in 4NCM and the configurations of its binding pocket.

steps.title: Recognize the cap
steps.text: The PB2 cap-binding pocket participates in recognition of capped RNA.

steps.title: Occupy the pocket
steps.text: The small molecule in 4NCM occupies the cap-binding pocket, illustrating how an inhibitor can interfere with cap recognition.

steps.title: Compare pocket configurations
steps.text: This work compares MD and OriDynamic ensembles around the bound ligand to show variation in pocket shape and local contacts.

reading.title: Scientific figure
reading.text: This protein–ligand case uses 4NCM. The MD–OriDynamic comparison, pocket-atom RMSF and PCA plots are results of this work. RMSF summarizes pocket-atom fluctuations, and both ensembles are projected onto the same MD-derived PCA axes. The 4NCM structural reference supports the inhibitor-bound domain, rather than these ensemble comparisons.

reading.title: Animation
reading.text: The cartoon introduces PB2, PA and PB1. The structural close-up then shows ligand occupancy and nearby aromatic and polar sites within the cap-binding pocket.

pb2-4ncm.interpretation: The displayed predictions are interpolated for viewing. Green proximity lines mark distances below 4 Å; a short distance alone does not establish a chemical bond.

fak-dd39.overview: Focal adhesion kinase is a protein kinase targeted by small-molecule inhibitors. The MD and OriDynamic ensembles illustrate ligand positions and contact patterns around its catalytic pocket.

steps.title: Occupy the kinase pocket
steps.text: Small molecules bind within the catalytic cleft and form contacts with the kinase domain.

steps.title: Reorganize contacts
steps.text: The displayed configurations span pocket-associated and more displaced ligand positions, with corresponding differences in protein–ligand contacts.

steps.title: Release the ligand
steps.text: The MD reference shows a ligand leaving the pocket. The cartoon illustrates the resulting free binding site and possible access by ATP.

reading.title: Scientific figure
reading.text: Compare the MD and OriDynamic ligand ensembles, the spatial distributions and selected residue contacts. S0–S3 close-ups highlight representative configurations from the FAK/DD39 analysis (Figure 6h).

reading.title: Animation
reading.text: The blue/gold predicted configurations are ordered by ligand displacement for display. The pink departure sequence is a chronological MD reference from one replica.

fak-dd39.interpretation: This comparison describes configurations and contacts. It does not establish a dissociation rate, residence time, or restoration of FAK activity after ligand release.
